originalTitle: Invitation Homes CEO says ban on institutional homebuying will bring down prices, but not immediately
summary: The CEO of the nation's largest single-family rental landlord said the new law banning large-scale investors from the market will lower prices in the long term.
content:
The CEO of Invitation Homes , the nation's largest single-family rental landlord, said he believes the recently passed housing bill that bans investors like him from buying existing homes will eventually lower home prices, but not in the short-term.

"I believe in the medium- to long-term, it definitely will," said Invitation Homes chief executive Dallas Tanner. "I think 90% of the bill focuses on deregulation. How do we simplify capital coming into housing? Are there ways that we can spur up the supply side challenges that we have? I think overnight in the immediate term, it's a bit trickier because there's more to the story than just what the bill addresses."

Tanner pointed to mortgage rate volatility, high construction costs, and zoning and regulatory imbalances.

In early January, President Donald Trump called for a ban on large-scale investors buying single-family homes to rent. He posted on social media that, "People live in homes, not corporations." This was part of a larger push to tackle the affordability crisis in housing. Some argued that institutional investors were pushing owner-occupants out of the market and inflating home prices.

The ban became law in July , preventing investors who own more than 350 homes from purchasing any more existing units. They can, however, buy new single-family homes specifically built for rent. That is where Invitation Homes is leaning in.

"Our focus as an industry and as a company has been, how do we create new supply and bring that into the housing system today? We built or acquired, in our partnerships with builders, over 6,000 new homes in the last five years," said Tanner.

In January, just weeks after Trump's post, Invitation Homes purchase a homebuilder, ResiBuilt. It has also purchased homes from large public builders like Pulte Homes and Lennar to use as rentals.

"We found through trial and error ... that this new product, this beta product, the product that we do amongst these master planned developments — it works really, really well for our families. And so we were indexing on that, and that is part of our growth strategy," said Tanner, adding that the company has been selling off hundreds of its older rental properties.

The largest investors, those owning more than 1,000 homes, represent less than 3% of the single-family rental market, according to various sources. They do, however, have an outsized footprint in certain metropolitan markets, like Atlanta (representing 25% of single-family homes there), Jacksonville (21%) and Charlotte (18%), according to the Urban institute.

Invitation Homes reported better-than-expected earnings at the end of July, even though rents and demand are not as healthy as they were in the first few years of the pandemic.

"We've seen sort of fundamentals reset. We talked about it on our last earnings call. We're starting to see actual pretty positive green shoots in several of our markets," said Tanner. "But we're really focused on — how do we navigate this and what does this mean?"
chineseTitle: Invitation Homes 首席执行官表示，禁止机构购房将降低价格，但不会立即降低
chineseSummary: 美国最大单户出租房东的首席执行官表示，禁止大规模投资者进入市场的新法律从长远来看将降低价格。
chineseContent:
美国最大的单户出租房东 Invitation Homes 的首席执行官表示，他相信最近通过的禁止像他这样的投资者购买现房的住房法案最终会降低房价，但短期内不会。

Invitation Homes 首席执行官达拉斯·坦纳 (Dallas Tanner) 表示：“我相信从中长期来看，它肯定会实现。” “我认为该法案 90% 的内容都集中在放松管制。我们如何简化资本进入住房市场？我们是否有办法加剧我们所面临的供给侧挑战？我认为短期内，这会有点棘手，因为故事的内容不仅仅是法案所解决的内容。”

坦纳指出了抵押贷款利率波动、建筑成本高昂以及分区和监管失衡等问题。

一月初，唐纳德·特朗普总统呼吁禁止大型投资者购买单户住宅用于出租。他在社交媒体上发帖称，“人们住在家里，而不是公司。”这是解决住房负担能力危机的更大努力的一部分。一些人认为，机构投资者正在将自住业主赶出市场并推高房价。

该禁令于 7 月成为法律，禁止拥有超过 350 套房屋的投资者购买更多现有单位。然而，他们可以购买专门为出租而建造的新单户住宅。这就是 Invitation Homes 所擅长的领域。

“作为一个行业和一家公司，我们的重点一直是如何创造新的供应并将其纳入当今的住房系统？在过去五年中，我们与建筑商合作建造或收购了 6,000 多套新房屋，”Tanner 说。

一月份，就在特朗普发表上述言论几周后，Invitation Homes 收购了一家住宅建筑商 ResiBuilt。它还从 Pulte Homes 和 Lennar 等大型公共建筑商那里购买了房屋用于出租。

“通过反复试验，我们发现这个新产品，这个测试版产品，我们在这些总体规划开发中所做的产品 - 它对我们的家庭来说真的非常好。所以我们对此进行了索引，这是我们增长战略的一部分，”坦纳说，并补充说该公司已经出售了数百套旧的出租房产。

据各种消息来源称，拥有 1,000 多套住房的最大投资者仅占单户租赁市场的不到 3%。然而，根据城市研究所的数据，它们在某些大都市市场确实占有很大的份额，例如亚特兰大（占那里单户住宅的 25%）、杰克逊维尔（21%）和夏洛特（18%）。

尽管租金和需求不如大流行最初几年那么健康，但 Invitation Homes 7 月底的盈利好于预期。

“我们已经看到了基本面的重置。我们在上次财报电话会议上谈到了这一点。我们开始看到我们的几个市场实际上出现了非常积极的萌芽，”坦纳说。 “但我们真正关注的是——我们如何应对这个问题，这意味着什么？”
